name: Makar Sankranti
description: The sun enters Capricorn. A fixed solar festival celebrated with kite flying, sesame sweets, and holy dips in sacred rivers.
significance: Marks the start of Uttarayana — the sun's northward journey. Bathing in the Ganga is especially meritorious. The day is auspicious for tarpan and charity.

name: Basant Panchami
description: The festival of spring and knowledge. Maa Saraswati is worshipped by students, artists, and scholars.
significance: The colour yellow is sacred — representing the mustard flowers of spring. Books and musical instruments are placed before the goddess for blessings.

name: Maha Shivaratri
description: The great night of Lord Shiva. All-night vigil, fasting, and continuous abhishek across all Shiva temples.
significance: Shiva lingams are bathed in milk, honey, and water through the night in four praharas. Devotees fast and chant Om Namah Shivaya without break.

name: Holi
description: The festival of colours. Preceded by Holika Dahan symbolising the victory of devotion over evil.
significance: Holika Dahan marks Prahlad's divine protection. Holi celebrates the eternal love of Radha-Krishna and the arrival of spring.

name: Ram Navami
description: Birth anniversary of Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram. Celebrated on Chaitra Shukla Navami with processions and Ramcharitmanas recitation.
significance: Ram's birth is celebrated with shobha yatras, recitation of Ramcharitmanas, and elaborate temple decorations across Bharat. Ayodhya sees lakhs of pilgrims.
mantra: श्री राम जय राम जय जय राम

name: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Hanuman — the embodiment of devotion, courage, and selfless service.
significance: Recitation of Hanuman Chalisa, Sundarkand, and Bajrang Baan. Red flowers, sindoor, and sesame oil are offered.

name: Akshaya Tritiya
description: One of the most auspicious days — any action begun or gift given on this day multiplies without end.
significance: Donations, new beginnings, and gold purchases are permanently blessed. The gates of Badrinath and Gangotri open on this day.

name: Ganga Dussehra
description: The day Goddess Ganga descended from the heavens to Earth. Massive bathing festivals along all Ganga ghats.
significance: A bath in the Ganga on this day cleanses ten types of sins. The water is especially potent. Ghats of Varanasi, Haridwar overflow with devotees.

name: Jagannath Rath Yatra
description: The grand chariot procession of Lord Jagannath from the main temple to Gundicha temple in Puri. One of the oldest and largest religious processions on Earth.
significance: Pulling the chariot of Lord Jagannath grants liberation equivalent to 100 sacrifices. Even a glimpse frees one from the cycle of rebirth.
rituals: Chhera pahanra by King of Puri

name: Guru Purnima
description: The full moon of Ashadha dedicated to honoring the Guru — birthdate of Maharishi Veda Vyasa, compiler of the Vedas.
significance: Disciples honor their gurus and spiritual masters. The day holds significance in Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions alike.

name: Raksha Bandhan
description: The sacred bond of siblings. Sisters tie a rakhi on their brother's wrist; brothers pledge lifelong protection.
significance: Raksha means protection, Bandhan means bond. The tradition originates from Draupadi tying cloth around Krishna's wrist.

name: Janmashtami
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Shri Krishna — celebrated at midnight with fasting, bhajans, jhanki darshan, and dahi handi.
significance: Krishna was born to liberate the world from Kamsa's tyranny. His birth is a cosmic event celebrated with ecstatic joy. Mathura and Vrindavan are transformed.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Ganesha — Vighnaharta, the remover of obstacles. A 10-day festival with grand clay idols and processions.
significance: Ganesha is invoked at the start of every ritual. His 10-day festival concludes with Ganesh Visarjan — immersion of the idol in water.

name: Pitru Paksha
description: Sixteen days dedicated to ancestor worship. Tarpan and shraddha performed at Gaya, Varanasi, and Prayagraj.
significance: During Pitru Paksha, the gates of Yamaloka open. Tarpan — water with sesame — offered to ancestors liberates them and brings blessings to the living.

name: Sharad Navratri
description: Nine nights of Maa Durga in her nine forms. The most celebrated Navratri — observed with fasting, garba, and Durga Saptashati recitation.
significance: The nine avatars worshipped are Shailputri through Siddhidatri. Culminates in Vijayadashami — the victory of good over evil.

name: Vijayadashami (Dussehra)
description: The day Maa Durga killed Mahishasura and Shri Ram killed Ravana. The ultimate triumph of good over evil.
significance: Considered the most auspicious day to begin new ventures. Ravana effigies are burned across Bharat. Mysore Dussehra is legendary.

name: Diwali & Dhanteras
description: The festival of lights. Shri Ram returned to Ayodhya after 14 years. The night Maa Lakshmi roams the earth entering well-lit, clean homes.
significance: Lakshmi-Ganesha puja at midnight on Amavasya. Dhanteras on Oct 20, Diwali on Oct 20. Five days of celebration with diyas, rangoli, and sweets.

name: Chhath Puja
description: The most spiritually intense Hindu festival. Devotees stand in rivers for hours offering arghya to the setting and rising sun — a 36-hour continuous fast.
significance: Chhath directly worships Surya Dev without any idol or intermediary. The river becomes the altar. The devotee stands as the priest. Raw faith, unmediated.

name: Dev Diwali
description: The Diwali of the Gods — on Kartik Purnima all 33 crore deities descend to the ghats of Varanasi. The entire riverfront illuminates with lakhs of diyas.
significance: Varanasi is the capital of Dev Diwali. Every ghat from Asi to Raj is lit with earthen lamps. The reflection of lakhs of flames in the Ganga is among the most extraordinary sights in Hinduism.
rituals: Ghat illumination with lakhs of diyas

name: Maha Shivaratri 2026
description: The great night of Lord Shiva in 2026. The cosmic marriage of Shiva and Parvati celebrated with all-night vigil, fasting, and continuous abhishek.
significance: Maha Shivaratri 2026 will see new significance with expanded Kashi Vishwanath Corridor and digital darshan reaching millions across the world.

name: Ganga Aarti — Dashashwamedh
description: Seven priests perform in perfect synchrony every evening at Dashashwamedh Ghat. Witnessed by thousands every single day without exception.
significance: The Ganga Aarti is a living ceremony continued without interruption for centuries. Every evening the boundary between the sacred and the everyday dissolves.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Aarti
description: Five aartis performed daily at the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga. Mangala Aarti at 3 AM draws thousands even before dawn.
significance: Shiva himself is said to reside in Kashi. The daily aarti is a direct communion with the divine — the most sacred Shiva darshan available to the world.
